activity.notes: William of Avesnes succeeded in 1304 not only as Count William I of Hainaut but also as Count William III of Holland. The County of Holland remained a distinct principality even while held in dynastic union with Hainaut and Zeeland, so ATLAS records the Holland comital authority as a separate concurrent Activity rather than leaving it folded into the Hainaut row.

sources.title: William III, Count of Holland and Hainaut — British Museum
sources.citation_text: The British Museum identifies William as Willem I van Henegouwen and Willem III van Holland and states that he was Count of Holland-Hainaut from 1304.

sources.title: Introduction — Postcolonial Fictions in the Roman de Perceforest
sources.citation_text: Cambridge identifies William I explicitly as Count of Hainaut, Holland, and Zeeland, confirming the simultaneous comital titles.
